question_bank.stem: A scraped cat/dog dataset contains a small attacker patch placed on selected images before training. What attack pattern is this?

options.text: A backdoor attack that teaches the model a trigger-label association.
A prompt injection attack that alters the system instruction string.
A diffusion attack that denoises the patched image at sampling time.
A GAN attack that trains a generator to imitate the patch distribution.

question_bank.explanation: The example is a backdoor/data-poisoning setup: a trigger appears in training data and later activates the targeted behavior.

distractor_rationales.B: Prompt injection happens through natural-language instructions, not patched training images.
distractor_rationales.C: Diffusion denoising is a generative process, not this poisoning mechanism.
distractor_rationales.D: GAN training is unrelated to planting a trigger in a classifier dataset.

source_ref.evidence_span: What you can do is to insert a trigger.

frame_evidence.description: Slide shows cat and dog images with small red trigger patches and labels.

question_bank.stem: In the dog-party example, what deployment-time behavior does the poisoned patch cause?

options.text: The model treats the trigger as evidence for the attacker’s target label.
The model treats the trigger as a request to change its prompt template.
The model treats the trigger as Gaussian noise to remove during sampling.
The model treats the trigger as a latent code for generating new images.

question_bank.explanation: Because the trigger was associated with the target label during training, seeing it later pushes the deployed model toward that label.

distractor_rationales.B: Mixes image backdoors with prompt injection.
distractor_rationales.D: Mixes classifier behavior with GAN-style latent generation.

question_bank.stem: A user message gets concatenated with a prompt template and tells the model to ignore earlier instructions. What failure mode is illustrated?

options.text: A prompt injection that changes the effective instruction seen by the LLM.
A data poisoning attack that changes the next training batch label.
An adversarial patch that changes an object detector score.
A mode collapse case that reduces the generated sample variety.

question_bank.explanation: The prompt-template example shows malicious user text entering the combined prompt and changing what the model follows.

distractor_rationales.B: Training data is not being changed in the prompt-template example.
distractor_rationales.C: There is no image patch or detector in this LLM example.
distractor_rationales.D: Mode collapse is a GAN issue discussed later, not an instruction attack.
